author: blu
body: Nothing caught it because a no-op looks like working code from every angle except an assertion on the result: it does not crash, the type is right, and the text comes back. These definitions were always correct, so the same call gave two answers depending on which chapter the caller cited. That is the duplicate-name hazard as a live defect rather than a warning, and it is why the rule is that CCE conversion happens at the I/O boundary and nowhere else. The duplicate is gone now and this chapter owns the pair; the account is kept here because the surviving implementation is the one it is about.

author: blu
body: These pad until the width is reached. They used to repeat the fill once per missing CHARACTER, which is the same thing only when the fill is one character long and wildly different otherwise: padding "a" to 5 with "xy" returned "xyxyxyxya", nine characters, because the deficit was four and the fill was appended four times. The prose two dozen lines above has always said "padded to the given width", so the body disagreed with its own chapter.

author: blu
body: It was never wrong in the tree -- every call site passes a single-character fill -- and it was invisible for the same reason. It surfaced only when this pair was run against the TextSearch pair it collided with, which had the pad-to-width behaviour, on a fill longer than one character. Same name, same signature, two different functions.
